name: ABCFair
description: Numerous methods have been implemented that pursue fairness with respect to sensitive features by mitigating biases in machine learning. Yet, the problem settings that each method tackles vary significantly, including the stage of intervention, the composition of sensitive features, the fairness notion, and the distribution of the output. Even in binary classification, these subtle differences make it highly complicated to benchmark fairness methods, as their performance can strongly depend on exactly how the bias mitigation problem was originally framed. Hence, we introduce ABCFair, a benchmark approach which allows adapting to the desiderata of the real-world problem setting, enabling proper comparability between methods for any use case. We apply ABCFair to a range of pre-, in-, and postprocessing methods on both large-scale, traditional datasets and on a dual label (biased and unbiased) dataset to sidestep the fairness-accuracy trade-off.
evaluation_method: accuracy combined with fairness metrics (e.g., demographic parity, equalized odds, fairness gap); reported as per-method tradeoffs
reputation: A recent research benchmark for fairness evaluation that is gaining attention in the fairness community but has limited broad adoption so far.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on fairness in classification; performance strongly depends on chosen fairness notion and intervention stage. Results are not directly comparable across different fairness problem framings; potential dataset biases and sensitivity to definition choices.
